accepted_source_properties: Imports exact hash-bound runner bytes with bytecode disabled and invokes only the isolated registry validator; subprocess run/Popen are explicitly denied.
Creates a fresh owned tiny fixture tree and tests 27 cases, including repeat acceptance of a terminal receipt plus legitimate two-record worker output that reproduces the old glob parser defect.

Rejects orphan output/pending, pending beside terminal receipt, each false or wrong-type cleanup flag, malformed/nonobject/wrong-schema/nonce/path/status/oversized receipt, unknown/uppercase names, directories and symlink entries.

Every case snapshots entry modes, sizes, regular-file digests and symlink targets before and after validation, so accepted classification cannot be achieved by deleting or rewriting retained evidence.

The report explicitly distinguishes synthetic flags from real process-exit proof, checks no native call attempted, rechecks runner source bytes, bounds each input at 32KiB and the final report at 128KiB, and refuses elapsed time beyond ten seconds.
execution_preconditions: Execute with exact reviewed fixture and R6 hashes, ordinary nonoptimized Python, a fresh owned directory and an external bounded watchdog.
Any timeout or missing durable receipt is failed/incomplete rather than passed. The internal elapsed checks alone do not preempt blocking filesystem IO.
This pure source/fixture scope proves receipt classification only; Windows process ownership still requires the separately accepted Windows helper fixture.
